title: The Bosphorus Brief — 28 August 2026
overview: A quiet news day for daily-life matters, but a busy one for legal and rights watchers: the European Court of Human Rights delivered a fresh Kavala ruling, Ankara eased visa rules for Syrian diplomats, and the lira's slow slide continues. Regional safety news is mostly steady, though the Iran-related conflict coverage keeps rumbling in the background.
sections: <parameter name="heading">ECHR and Kavala: another ruling, same standoff
body: Jurist.org reports the European Court of Human Rights has again found that Türkiye violated Osman Kavala's rights to free speech and assembly. Separately, Nordic Monitor (opposition-leaning) describes friction between the ECHR and Türkiye's own Constitutional Court over which body has final say in such cases, noting pushback from a Turkish judge. For foreign residents, the practical takeaway is limited but worth noting: this is part of a longer pattern of tension between domestic and European judicial oversight that shapes how civil-liberty cases are ultimately resolved here.
